bull.label: Bull

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values OneSource: three of the four brokers that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA (ICICI Securities a sum of the parts at 19x DDC and 16x soft gel and injectables FY28E EBITDA, Sep-2026; JM Financial 22x Sep-27E, Nov-2025; Investec 23x FY27E, May-2025); DAM Capital uses 30x FY28E EPS; SBICAP states no method. 16.5x = OneSource's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 13-May-2026 (listed 24-Jan-2025; the window starts at the Q4FY26 results, the first of the profitable quarters after the Q3FY26 loss, and the forward year is FY28E throughout; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 21 points; EV = market value + the last published company net debt excl. leases, as in the engine; forward EBITDA = our FY28E, before exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 16.8x x 0.983 (nine pharma peers' trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced −1.7%) = 16.5x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net debt. Bull 17x / bear 16x = 75th / 25th percentile (17.2x / 16.3x) x 0.983. Trough test on EBITDA: FY28E is far above half the best of FY24-26 (FY25 Rs467 cr); none. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by ONESOURCE.mult.js.

cover.headline: India's GLP-1 fill-finish leader at the start of its ramp: on its own post-turnaround EV/EBITDA the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}}, a BUY, even with the ramp a year late
cover.lead: OneSource Specialty Pharma is a Bengaluru contract manufacturer formed in 2024 from three Strides-group businesses: drug-device combinations (it fills and assembles generic GLP-1 pens and cartridges), biologics, sterile injectables and soft gelatin capsules. It fills all three generic semaglutide approvals in Canada and ~40% of India's generic pens, and is tripling its cartridge capacity by FY28. Q1FY27 revenue rose 37% to ₹449 cr after a loss-making FY26. We forecast EBITDA of ₹{{F.ebitda.0|num}} / {{F.ebitda.1|num}} / {{F.ebitda.2|num}} cr for FY27-29E, 15-40% below the street for FY27-28 because we assume the plan runs a year late. Three of the four brokers that disclose a method use **EV/EBITDA**, and so do we: OneSource's median forward EV/EBITDA since the Q4FY26 results (16.8x), adjusted −1.7% for the pharma sector over the same window, gives **16.5x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,326 cr = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with BUY**. Cross-checks: P/E ₹1,824; DCF ₹1,678. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: A head start in the scarcest part of generic GLP-1s
arguments.p: Sterile fill-finish and pen assembly take ~2 years to build; OneSource built early, got its customers' products filed on its site and reserved capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay terms. Line 2 starts in Q2FY27, line 3 within FY27, a fourth in FY28: sterile days rise from 225 to 675.

arguments.h: The ramp has started, a year late
arguments.p: FY26 was guided at ~30% growth and fell 2% when Canadian approvals slipped; Q3FY26 EBITDA was ₹17 cr. Since then: India and Canada launches, Q1FY27 revenue +37%, EBITDA margin 27.5%. We assume FY28 revenue ~18% below the US$400m target and reach it only in FY29E.

arguments.h: Governance is the discount the multiple must carry
arguments.p: Strides-group companies are ~28% of revenue and several cost lines; 37% of the promoters' 30.5% stake is pledged; the promoter group sold ~8 points after listing; a share-funded purchase of promoter-owned businesses was dropped only after minorities objected. A US$136m arbitration claim is unprovided.

arguments.h: A fair multiple, not a stretched one
arguments.p: ₹1,522 is 55.1x trailing but 15.9x our FY28E EBITDA. We use the stock's own post-turnaround multiple with no sector lift; P/E and DCF agree within ~10%. The rule turns HOLD above ~₹1,600.

sections.title: A Bengaluru contract manufacturer for complex products: GLP-1 pens and cartridges are the growth engine, soft gels and sterile injectables the base, biologics the option

blocks.p: OneSource is a CDMO (contract development and manufacturing organisation): it develops and makes medicines that other companies own and sell. It does four things. (1) **Drug-device combinations (DDC)**: it fills peptide drugs such as generic semaglutide (Ozempic/Wegovy) and liraglutide into cartridges, pre-filled syringes and vials, inspects them, assembles them into pens, labels and packs them, end to end. The customer usually supplies the active ingredient; OneSource earns a development fee while a product is being filed (MSA, master service agreement) and a conversion fee per unit once it is approved (CSA, commercial supply agreement). (2) **Biologics**: drug substance (microbial 1KL, mammalian 2 x 2KL) and drug product on one site, for biosimilar makers, innovators and animal-health companies; still mostly development work. (3) **Sterile injectables**: vials and syringes, including one of few USFDA-approved penicillin fill-finish plants, focused on products in shortage. (4) **Oral technologies**: soft gelatin capsules (2.4bn a year), until 2024 made mainly for Strides' own brands. It has five sites in Bengaluru, ~1,600 people and 80+ customers.

blocks.callout: **So what:** OneSource is a capacity business at an inflection. For two years it sold scarce GLP-1 fill-finish capacity in advance (development fees, reservation fees), and the money now depends on how many pens its partners sell once their approvals arrive. The base business is steady but tied to the founder's other companies, and biologics will not earn commercial revenue before FY29.

sections.title: Built from three Arun Kumar companies in 2024, listed in Jan-2025 without an IPO; a related-party acquisition was announced and then withdrawn

blocks.p: OneSource began as the biotech arm of the Strides group (Stelis Biopharma, a biologics venture whose terminated Sputnik Light vaccine contract is still in arbitration). Its founder, Arun Kumar, built Strides, sold its injectables business Agila to Mylan for US$1.6bn in 2013 and re-entered injectables through Steriscience after the non-compete ended. A scheme announced in Sep-2023 merged Strides' soft-gel CDMO business and Steriscience's injectables CDMO business into Stelis, renamed OneSource; it took effect on 1-Apr-2024 (NCLT order 14-Nov-2024). Strides shareholders received OneSource shares, so the stock listed on 24-Jan-2025 without an IPO; ₹801 cr had been raised privately in Nov-2024 at a ~US$1.65bn valuation.

blocks.callout: **Lesson from history:** OneSource is a Strides-family construct, and that cuts both ways. The founder's deal-making record (Agila) and relationships brought customers and investors quickly. But the same family owns its biggest customer group, its landlord and the businesses it tried to buy; and the first act of the promoter group after listing was to sell about a fifth of its stake.

sections.title: Industry: generic semaglutide opens market by market from 2026; capacity, not demand, is the constraint for now; the US and Europe only open from ~2031

blocks.p: Semaglutide (Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Wegovy) is the largest drug going off patent outside the US and Europe. The markets losing protection by mid-2026 sold ~US$4.1 bn of the brand in 2025 (IQVIA, in OneSource's deck), led by Canada (US$2.2bn) and Brazil (US$0.8bn); the brand was scarce in most of them, so generics are expanding the market rather than just replacing it (India: from <2,000 to 150,000-160,000 generic pens a month within a year). Generic companies need sterile fill-finish and pen-assembly capacity that takes about two years to build, which is why OneSource could reserve its line years ahead. Fill-finish and device assembly for generic GLP-1s: Indian generic majors building own capacity, global CDMOs and device makers; a listed peer is expanding from 40m to 140m devices (Q2FY26 call); OneSource's customers have first right of refusal to match prices in markets like Canada (Chairman, Jan-2026).

blocks.callout: **So what:** the near-term market is real but smaller than the GLP-1 headlines suggest: the US and Europe, by far the largest markets, stay closed until ~2031. Until then OneSource's volumes come from Canada, India, Brazil and other emerging markets, at falling generic prices. The open question is price: once generic capacity is no longer scarce (management itself says the supply gap lasts "at least for next 2 years"), conversion fees will compete, which is why our steady-state margin sits below the guided 40%.

sections.title: Drug-device combinations: one sold-out cartridge line becomes three; FY28 depends on emerging-market volumes and on keeping customers once capacity is no longer scarce

blocks.p: The DDC business fills peptide drugs into cartridges and syringes and assembles them into pens, for 20+ customers and 50+ projects (seven variants of liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide generics, plus small-molecule and biologic DDCs). Until Q1FY27 everything ran on one line with ~225 sterile production days a year and a 200-litre batch limit; it was "fully committed back-to-back" and OneSource stopped accepting new customers. The US$100m programme adds a second line (commercial in Q2FY27) and a third (installed within FY27), each able to run 500-1,000-litre batches, and a fourth later in FY28: 675 sterile days in FY28 against 225 in FY26, and up to 2.5x more pens per day on the bigger batches. Line 1 reached its full revenue contribution in Q1FY27 (CEO). Customers reserve capacity with upfront fees and take-or-pay terms, but in Jan-2026 the Chairman said some take-or-pay obligations were deferred in exchange for longer contracts.

sections.title: The base business: a steady ~₹800 cr of sterile injectables and soft gels, much of it sold to the Strides group; new capacity from FY28

blocks.p: The base business came from the 2024 merger. **Sterile injectables** (the former Steriscience CDMO business) makes vials and pre-filled syringes at the SPD site, focusing on products that are often in short supply in the US, and runs a dedicated USFDA-approved penicillin fill-finish plant under a tolling agreement with the site operator (a top-5 penicillin supplier to the US in its molecules). A ~4-month shutdown in Q2-Q3FY27 adds lyophilisation, long-acting injectables and high-viscosity PFS capacity, which management expects to matter from FY28. **Soft gelatin capsules** were Strides' captive plant (Strides' brands are still the largest buyer: Strides-group entities bought ₹372 cr of goods in FY26). Capacity was tripled to 2.4bn capsules a year; OneSource now sells to third parties (tech transfers from European sites, a first oncology NDA with a top-10 US generic company) and expects the plant to be full in 12-24 months, after which it needs a greenfield site; the current site is shared with Strides under a limited-period transition agreement, for which OneSource paid Strides ₹88 cr of process and conversion charges in FY26.

blocks.p: The flagship site is one of few globally that make biologic drug substance (microbial 1KL; mammalian 2 x 2KL single-use) and fill the drug product on the same site. The funnel of requests for proposal is ~4x a year earlier, helped by new US and EU biosimilar guidance and the BIOSECURE Act. FY26-27 wins: a European biosimilar developer, a US biosimilar major (5+ products), Formycon (Germany), a second project with a top-3 animal-health company. All are development (MSA) work now; management expects commercial manufacturing from FY29 and plans +5KL microbial and +4KL mammalian capacity, "significantly lower" in cost than the DDC programme. Management will not say whether biologics is profitable yet.

sections.title: Competitive advantage: a head start in GLP-1 fill-finish and a clean regulatory record; no scale advantage and a moat that narrows as capacity arrives

blocks.p: A moat is a lasting advantage that lets a company earn more than its cost of capital for longer than rivals. OneSource has a lead, which is not quite the same thing. It built GLP-1 cartridge and pen capacity before the rush, qualified it with regulators (USFDA, EU, Health Canada, ANVISA) and got its customers' products filed on its site; switching a filed product costs a customer time and new filings. But fill-finish and assembly are not secret technology, generic majors are building their own lines, and management itself says the supply gap lasts "at least for next 2 years".

blocks.p: OneSource's quarters move with its customers' regulatory calendar. When development (MSA) work is billed, margins are high (Q4FY25 EBITDA margin 43%); when the cartridge line waits for approvals, revenue and margin collapse (Q3FY26: revenue ₹290 cr, margin 6%). With semaglutide launches in India (Mar-2026) and Canada (from May-2026), Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 recovered to ₹428 cr and ₹449 cr. The base business has a seasonal tilt: soft-gel demand (cold and flu products) is H2-heavy, so the second half is normally stronger (CEO, 25-Jul-2026).

blocks.p: OneSource's comparable history is short. The merger that created it took effect on 1-Apr-2024, so FY25 is its first full year; Screener's earlier columns are Stelis Biopharma alone (FY24 revenue ₹172 cr; we drop FY21-23 and show FY24 only as the pre-demerger year), and the company's own pro-forma FY24 for the combined business was revenue ₹1,082 cr and EBITDA ₹225 cr. FY25 revenue rose to ₹1,445 cr with EBITDA of ₹467 cr (32%), lifted by development (MSA) fees from GLP-1 customers preparing their filings. FY26 was meant to be the year commercial supply began; it was not. Canadian semaglutide approvals slipped by one to two quarters, OneSource stopped taking new DDC development work to keep its one cartridge line free for commercial orders, and Q3FY26 revenue fell 26% with EBITDA of only ₹17 cr. FY26 revenue ended 2% lower at ₹1,422 cr and EBITDA 35% lower at ₹304 cr (21%), while employee and other costs rose ahead of the new lines. Reported profit was a loss in both years: depreciation of ~₹275-280 cr includes ₹138 cr a year of amortisation of intangibles created by the merger, and finance costs were ₹122-166 cr.

blocks.p: OneSource raised ₹801 cr of equity before listing (Nov-2024) and used it to prepay expensive debt and start its US$100m capex programme. Credit ratings have risen five notches since listing into the 'A' category and the borrowing cost is below 9%.

blocks.p: Three of the four brokers that disclose a method value OneSource on **EV/EBITDA** (ICICI Securities: a sum of the parts at 19x DDC and 16x soft gel and injectables FY28E EBITDA; JM Financial 22x Sep-27E; Investec 23x FY27E); DAM Capital uses 30x FY28E EPS. EV/EBITDA also suits the company: profit after tax is still distorted by ₹138 cr a year of merger amortisation, heavy interest and tax losses, none of which touch EBITDA. We follow the majority: **EV/EBITDA on Sep-28E EBITDA (half FY28E, half FY29E) less Sep-28E net debt**. P/E and a DCF are cross-checks.

blocks.h: Our target multiple: 16.5x, and why the window starts on 13-May-2026

blocks.p: OneSource listed on 24-Jan-2025 and is a turnaround, so it has neither a five-year history nor a clean one. We start its own window **on 13-May-2026, the day the Q4FY26 results were published**: (1) it skips the post-listing months; (2) it is the first result after the Q3FY26 loss, and the quarters since (Q4FY26 PAT ₹4.6 cr, Q1FY27 ₹25 cr) are the first run of profitable quarters as a combined company: the break to sustained profits; (3) throughout the window the next full year is FY28E, the first year with all three cartridge lines, so every point is measured on post-ramp EBITDA. Earlier points mislead: from the FY25 results (5-May-2025) to Mar-2026 the forward year was FY27, a ramp-up year (our FY27E EBITDA is 58% of FY28E), so the stock traded at 31.1x forward EBITDA while the market was paying for FY28-29 capacity; applying that multiple to Sep-28E EBITDA would count the ramp twice. The trough rule, tested on EBITDA, excludes nothing (FY28E is far above half of FY25's ₹467 cr). On every weekly close plus the 30-Sep-2026 close (21 points), EV = market value + the last published company net debt (excluding leases, like the engine), over our FY28E EBITDA (before exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same). We multiply the median by the nine pharma peers' EV/EBITDA move over the **same window** (−1.7%) and round to the nearest half-turn. The window is short (4.5 months); the alternatives are sensitivity rows below.

sections.title: Our honest summary: scarce GLP-1 capacity bought at a price that already assumes most of the ramp; BUY on our slower ramp, with governance the main reason not to pay more

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** the CDMO that fills every generic semaglutide approval in Canada and ~40% of India's generic pens, with capacity tripling by FY28, a clean regulatory record and options in biologics and tirzepatide. **What you are not buying:** a proven earnings stream (reported losses in FY25-26), independence from the founder's other companies (~28% of revenue), or a moat that survives once fill-finish capacity is plentiful.

**What you are paying:** ₹1,522 is 55.1x trailing EBITDA but 15.9x our FY28E. On the street's method (EV/EBITDA), OneSource's own 16.8x median since the turnaround (13-May-2026), × 0.983 for the sector, gives 16.5x Sep-28E EBITDA of ₹1,326 cr = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): a BUY under the house rule. P/E (₹1,824) and DCF (₹1,678) agree within ~10%. The upside is the ramp being delivered, even a year late; it is not a re-rating.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for OneSource Specialty Pharma (consolidated, Rs crore). FY21-23 (Stelis alone) dropped and FY26 PAT/EPS put on the 30-Sep-2026 share count by tools/authoring/ONESOURCE.patch.js; FY24 is pre-demerger. OneSource reports one segment and no modality split; the engine runs one revenue-growth path and the two-line build (DDC & biologics; base business of sterile injectables and soft gels) sits in businessLines, checked against model revenue in ONESOURCE.ctx.js. EBITDA is before other income (company and Screener agree). Depreciation includes the Rs137.8 cr a year of scheme amortisation in history and forecasts alike. OneSource has net debt: other income and interest are built in ONESOURCE.ctx.js and written here by ONESOURCE.mult.js. Valued on EV/EBITDA, the method most brokers that disclose one use.
assumptions._revenueWhy: Sum of the two-line build below. FY27E +51%: Q1FY27 revenue Rs449 cr (+37%); the second cartridge line is commercial from Q2 (doubling sterile production days) and the third is installed within FY27; management promises sequential growth every quarter, with H2 stronger, but a ~4-month shutdown at one sterile-injectables site falls in Q2-Q3. Our FY27E needs Q2-Q4 revenue of ~Rs1,700 cr (~Rs567 cr a quarter, a Q4 exit of ~Rs640 cr). FY28E +45% and FY29E +22%: three DDC lines (675 sterile days), larger batch sizes, Brazil and other emerging markets, biologics MSAs; FY28E Rs3,118 cr is ~18% below the US$400m guidance (~Rs3,780 cr at Rs94.5/US$): FY26 was guided at ~30% growth and fell 2%, so we assume the ramp runs about a year behind plan. Street FY27E Rs2,354-2,803 cr, FY28E Rs3,407-3,762 cr (ICICI Securities 6-Sep-2026, SBICAP 5-Jan-2026, JM 6-May-2025).

base._why: GAM estimate: the company discloses no split. 'Our soft gels and injectables business are trending closer to the US$100 million mark' (Chairman, 13-May-2026) = ~Rs800-900 cr at Rs89.9/US$; soft gels sold to Strides-group entities alone were Rs371.5 cr in FY26 (AR note 32). We put the base business at Rs800 cr and DDC & biologics (incl. MSA development income) at the remaining Rs622 cr of FY26 revenue of Rs1,422 cr (Screener; AR Rs1,421.6 cr).

businessLines._why: Base business (sterile injectables incl. penicillin, soft gels) +6% in FY27E (four-month shutdown at one sterile site for lyophilisation and high-viscosity PFS; soft-gel capacity tripled to 2.4bn and fills over 12-15 months as tech transfers land), +18% in FY28E (the new injectables capacity for a full year; soft gel full), +12% in FY29E (greenfield soft-gel plant not before FY29-30). DDC & biologics is the balance: ~2.1x in FY27E (line 1 at full revenue in Q1; line 2 from Q2; India and Canada semaglutide, liraglutide, other peptides), +63% in FY28E (three lines, 500L batches, Brazil and MENA), +27% in FY29E (fourth line; biologics commercial supply starts; US and Europe still closed).

assumptions._marginWhy: FY26 21.4% (6% in Q3FY26 on delayed Canadian approvals; 21.5% in Q4); Q1FY27 27.5%: line 1 at full revenue, but the opex for lines 2-3 and 380+ hires is already in the base (CEO, 25-Jul-2026). FY27E 31.5%: quarterly margins rising from 27.5% to ~36% as the new lines fill (operating leverage), less the injectables shutdown. FY28E 37.5% and FY29E 39%: close to but below the guided ~40% steady state (FY25 reached 32% on MSA-heavy revenue; Q4FY25 43%). FY26 EBITDA included a Rs31.4 cr forex gain inside other expenses; we forecast none. Street FY27E 38.7-40.0%, FY28E 40.0-41.3%.
assumptions._capexWhy: FY26 Rs569 cr (AR cash flow); US$100m DDC programme ~80% committed by Jul-2026 (capital commitments Rs282 cr at Mar-26); FY27E Rs450 cr = third line and the balance of the programme, injectables upgrade, soft-gel greenfield start; FY28E Rs400 cr = fourth DDC line and biologics (+5KL microbial, +4KL mammalian, 'significantly lower than DDC'); FY29E Rs350 cr. Karnataka incentive (~Rs70 cr) not netted.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs279 cr: PPE Rs78.9 cr, right-of-use Rs23.7 cr, intangibles Rs176.5 cr (of which scheme amortisation Rs137.8 cr, which continues to FY34). Q1FY27 Rs72 cr. Screener's gross block (Rs6,799 cr) includes goodwill, so the rate is a calibration: 4.35% gives ~Rs305 / 324 / 341 cr in FY27-29E as lines 2-4 are commissioned.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Net debt: no treasury book. Interest on the operating cash buffer is built in ONESOURCE.ctx.js and entered in otherIncome.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Built from sourced parts (ONESOURCE.ctx.js): 6.5% on an operating cash and margin-money buffer of ~Rs100 cr (Mar-26 cash Rs35.7 cr + other bank balances Rs61.9 cr; CARE: ~Rs100 cr at Dec-25) = Rs6.5 cr; unwinding of discount on security deposits Rs0.7 cr; scrap sales Rs0.6 cr; support-service income from promoter-group entities Rs1.8 cr (AR note 21). FY26 Rs15.0 cr earned interest of Rs11.0 cr on a larger average cash balance (Rs301 cr at Mar-25), plus one-offs.
assumptions._interestWhy: Built in ONESOURCE.ctx.js: 8.25% on average gross borrowings (engine net debt + a Rs100 cr cash buffer; effective cost 'below 9%', CFO 13-May-2026) + Rs20 cr lease interest + Rs10 cr guarantee and bank charges, less Rs10 cr capitalised in FY27E. FY26 finance cost Rs122.2 cr (AR note 24); Q1FY27 Rs31 cr.
assumptions._taxWhy: OneSource carries Rs447.6 cr of unrecognised deferred tax assets on unabsorbed losses and depreciation (AR note 34) and booked a tax credit in Q1FY27 (PBT Rs20 cr, PAT Rs25 cr); it has not yet opted for the 25.17% regime. FY27E 10% and FY28E 15% (MAT-type current tax while losses are used); FY29E 25.2% (conservative: unused losses could shelter part of FY29).
assumptions._payoutWhy: No dividend so far; capex is debt-funded.

dcf._betaWhy: The engine discounts at the cost of equity; beta 1.05 gives 12.8%, ~our WACC (cost of equity ~13%, net debt ~6% of EV at ~6.5% after tax): customer concentration, a two-year track record and a single-product ramp.
dcf._tgWhy: 5.5%: middle of the house 5-6% range; GLP-1 volumes keep growing but CDMO prices fall as capacity arrives.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: From 22% (FY29E) to 7% by FY42E: US and Europe semaglutide from ~FY31-32, tirzepatide later, biologics commercial supply from FY29.
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: 37%, below the guided 40%: more commercial (CSA) than MSA revenue and price competition in fill-finish.
dcf._wcNote: Engine operating working capital is 31.4% of FY26 sales (Screener Mar-26: other assets less cash, less other liabilities, which include Rs227.6 cr of lease liabilities). True operating working capital excluding leases was ~47% of FY26 sales and ~37% of Q1FY27 annualised revenue (receivables 177 days; customer-funded inventory); management expects it to normalise in FY27. Treating leases as debt and normalising working capital to ~33% gives almost the same Sep-28E net debt (see report).

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: The ramp runs to plan: lines 2-3 fill in FY27, Dr Reddy's resumes quickly, Brazil and MENA approvals arrive early and batch sizes rise; FY28 revenue reaches ~US$360-370m and the margin ~39.5%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: A repeat of FY26: approvals slip again, a large partner's supply stays disrupted and generic semaglutide prices squeeze CDMO volumes or rates; growth runs ~12 points a year slower and the margin stays ~3 points lower.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: How the street values OneSource: three of the four brokers that disclose a method use EV/EBITDA (ICICI Securities a sum of the parts at 19x DDC and 16x soft gel and injectables FY28E EBITDA, Sep-2026; JM Financial 22x Sep-27E, Nov-2025; Investec 23x FY27E, May-2025); DAM Capital uses 30x FY28E EPS; SBICAP states no method. 16.5x = OneSource's median one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 13-May-2026 (listed 24-Jan-2025; the window starts at the Q4FY26 results, the first of the profitable quarters after the Q3FY26 loss, and the forward year is FY28E throughout; every weekly close plus the 30-Sep close, 21 points; EV = market value + the last published company net debt excl. leases, as in the engine; forward EBITDA = our FY28E, before exceptional items, so the pre-exceptional and reported medians are the same) of 16.8x x 0.983 (nine pharma peers' trailing EV/EBITDA at the 30-Sep close vs their medians over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced −1.7%) = 16.5x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EBITDA plus Sep-28E net debt. Bull 17x / bear 16x = 75th / 25th percentile (17.2x / 16.3x) x 0.983. Trough test on EBITDA: FY28E is far above half the best of FY24-26 (FY25 Rs467 cr); none. No own-move blend, no growth uplift (sensitivities only). Written by ONESOURCE.mult.js.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Cross-check: OneSource's median one-year-forward P/E since 13-May-2026 (same weekly closes; forward EPS = our FY28E, reported basis incl. the Rs137.8 cr scheme amortisation, no exceptional items) of 30.2x x 0.994 (the nine peers' P/E move over the same window, PLAYBOOK §7c; reproduced −0.6%) = 30.0x, nearest half-turn, on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 31x / bear 29x = 75th / 25th percentile x 0.994. DAM Capital: 30x FY28E EPS.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 12.8% (cost of equity ~ WACC; net debt is small against market value), terminal growth 5.5%, less engine net debt at Mar-27E.
